name: JavaScript
guidance: Respect the project's module format and supported runtime; validate external data at boundaries.

name: TypeScript
guidance: Keep types meaningful and check public boundaries; avoid weakening type checks to hide failures.

name: Python
guidance: Follow the existing Python environment and dependency conventions; isolate environments and verify changed behavior.

name: Rust
guidance: Use explicit error handling and ownership boundaries; avoid panics in normal failure paths.

name: C
guidance: Make memory ownership and bounds explicit; preserve the supported compiler and platform contracts.

name: C++
guidance: Prefer explicit ownership and existing build conventions; check lifetime and cross-platform behavior.

name: C#
guidance: Respect nullable annotations and the selected runtime; follow the existing solution and project structure.

name: Java
guidance: Use the established Java toolchain and dependency management; keep resource lifetimes and exceptions clear.

name: Kotlin
guidance: Respect nullability and coroutine ownership; preserve target-platform compatibility.

name: Swift
guidance: Preserve deployment targets and explicit concurrency ownership; verify platform availability before adopting APIs.

name: Go
guidance: Handle errors and cancellation explicitly; follow the module's existing conventions.

name: PHP
guidance: Preserve the supported PHP runtime and dependency setup; validate request input and escape rendered output.

name: Ruby
guidance: Follow the project's dependency and test conventions; keep external input validation explicit.

name: Dart
guidance: Respect sound null safety and existing asynchronous error handling.

name: Lua
guidance: Check the actual host runtime and Lua version; avoid assuming libraries available in a different embedding.

name: Scala
guidance: Preserve the project's Scala version and build conventions; keep effects and error handling clear.

name: R
guidance: Keep analyses reproducible and document data assumptions; preserve the established package environment.

name: Elixir
guidance: Use the existing supervision and process boundaries; test failure and recovery behavior.

name: Haskell
guidance: Follow the package's compiler and effect conventions; keep partial operations out of normal failure paths.

name: Zig
guidance: Verify the project's Zig toolchain; make allocators, ownership and error handling explicit.

name: HTML
guidance: Use semantic elements and accessible names; preserve keyboard navigation.

name: CSS
guidance: Preserve responsive layouts, readable contrast and visible keyboard focus.

name: Sass
guidance: Follow existing stylesheet boundaries and compilation conventions.

name: React
guidance: Keep state ownership clear and effects focused on synchronization; preserve accessible interaction.

name: Vue
guidance: Follow existing component and reactivity conventions; keep state and accessible interaction predictable.

name: Svelte
guidance: Inspect the project's Svelte version and component conventions before changing reactivity.

name: Angular
guidance: Preserve the existing Angular architecture and dependency injection boundaries.

name: Next.js
guidance: Inspect the router and deployment target; keep server and client boundaries explicit.

name: Nuxt
guidance: Inspect the rendering and deployment setup; preserve server and client boundaries.

name: Astro
guidance: Respect static and server rendering boundaries and add client-side hydration only where needed.

name: Vite
guidance: Follow the existing build setup; treat client environment variables as public output.

name: Web platform
guidance: Use semantic, accessible UI and preserve responsive behavior across supported browsers.

name: Tauri
guidance: Keep native commands narrowly scoped and validated; preserve capability restrictions and supported desktop platforms.

name: Electron
guidance: Keep renderer privileges narrow and validate IPC at the main-process boundary.

name: .NET
guidance: Preserve target frameworks and supported operating systems; use the established solution structure.

name: ASP.NET Core
guidance: Preserve middleware and authorization ordering; validate input and keep secrets outside source control.

name: Flutter
guidance: Preserve platform support, accessible widgets and existing state ownership.

name: React Native
guidance: Verify native-platform capabilities and preserve accessible behavior on every supported target.

name: Unity
guidance: Preserve asset GUIDs and the selected render pipeline; verify changes in the project's Editor version.

name: Godot
guidance: Preserve scene and resource references; inspect the engine version before adopting APIs.

name: Node.js
guidance: Respect the project's package manager, module format and supported runtime; keep server secrets outside client bundles.

name: Deno
guidance: Follow the project's task and import conventions; request only the permissions the application requires.

name: Bun
guidance: Inspect the actual runtime and package scripts; verify compatibility before assuming Node.js behavior.

name: FastAPI
guidance: Validate API schemas and keep blocking work out of asynchronous request handlers.

name: Django
guidance: Preserve authentication and migration conventions; test schema changes and avoid production-data assumptions.

name: Flask
guidance: Follow the existing application lifecycle and configuration boundaries; validate requests and protect secrets.

name: Express
guidance: Keep middleware ordering, request validation and error handling explicit.

name: NestJS
guidance: Preserve module and dependency injection boundaries; validate external inputs.

name: Spring Boot
guidance: Respect configuration profiles and transaction boundaries; verify database migrations and authorization.

name: Laravel
guidance: Preserve framework conventions, authorization checks and migration history.

name: Ruby on Rails
guidance: Preserve framework conventions and migration history; validate authorization and data boundaries.

name: Phoenix
guidance: Preserve context and supervision boundaries; verify database and real-time behavior.

name: SQLite
guidance: Preserve data and migration history; account for connection lifetime, locking and backup behavior.

name: PostgreSQL
guidance: Use parameterized queries and explicit migrations; preserve transactional and data-integrity guarantees.

name: MySQL
guidance: Use parameterized queries and explicit migrations; verify collation and transaction assumptions.

name: MongoDB
guidance: Validate document boundaries, indexes and schema evolution against observed workloads.

name: Redis
guidance: Make expiration, persistence and eviction expectations explicit; do not assume cached values are permanent.

name: Cloudflare Workers
guidance: Inspect the project's Cloudflare configuration and bindings; distinguish local verification from deployment and preserve runtime limits.

name: Cloudflare Pages
guidance: Inspect actual build and deployment configuration; keep production deployment an explicit user action.

name: Docker
guidance: Keep credentials outside image layers and source; preserve runtime user, volume and networking assumptions.

name: GitHub Actions
guidance: Keep workflow permissions narrow, protect secrets and distinguish verification from publishing.

name: Vercel
guidance: Inspect deployment and environment settings; do not assume preview and production configuration are interchangeable.

name: Netlify
guidance: Inspect build, redirects and environment settings; keep production publishing an explicit action.
